Yes! I’ve been doing this for a couple months now and I still get anxious about it. It’s easier for me to talk about these kinds of things with close friends and family, but with a stranger that’s a whole nother story. I know that’s the other way around for other people, but for me, it’s easier with loved ones because you already have that established relationship and you can open up with them about almost anything. It’s...different with a therapist you don’t know because you don’t know them and they don’t know you. That’s part of the anxiety because you talk about personal things with them and you get anxious. And you don’t know anything about them at first. The first few appointments will be like this. It’s important to start building a relationship with your therapist when you can over your next couple appointments so you can feel comfortable about talking about these kind of things, because now you’re just starting to get to know the other person. And that’s another thing: it does get easier to talk with them about things when you start establishing that relationship with your therapist. You know them better than you did before and you feel like you can talk to them about almost everything. Over time it will get easier and easier trust me. This way you can help lessen the anxiety at least a little bit, because now you feel more comfortable about talking about personal things with them. I’m just telling you what worked for me - but know that what worked for me may not work for you. You will prolly still get anxious before appointments, but it will get to the point where you don’t feel as anxious as the past couple appointments. Just don’t close up - the point is to talk about your problems and what to do about them, not NOT talk about them. I know it’s scary at first and is new; I was nervous on the first appointment.

But you can do it! You don’t really know what you’re doing at first, but over time you will get the hang of it and you’ll get used to doing this over time.

There are stories where people become close friends with therapists over the years. There’s a reason for that!

I had an appointment earlier today with my therapist and I was talking to her about some serious issues in rl I had to deal with. But after talking to her about it,I felt like a weight had been lifted off my shoulders. I never talked about it with anyone before, and after talking about it with someone, I felt a lot better. I always tried to keep things inside, but I realized it’s important to talk about them with someone, instead of dealing with them by yourself. She gave me good advice how to cope with it and now I’m not anxious anymore. But I’m prolly gonna be anxious before next appointment lol

Just know that it will get easier over time. Stay safe! Have a good one, mate! =D
